lines.en: label ramen25:
scene tsuneyogreenonion1
: Sigh.
: You’re not supposed to say “sigh,” Tsuneyo. You’re supposed to just...actually do it.
: Sensei, when you look at this knife...what do you see?
: A knife.
: Look closer.
scene tsuneyogreenonion2
: It’s still a knife.
: Precisely.
scene tsuneyogreenonion3
: What?
: Sometimes, what you see is what you get.
: And other times, you get a knife.
: Tsuneyo, what the fuck are you talking about?
: Knives, idiot.
: I had a thought, but it went somewhere else.
: This would not be an issue if you were more entertaining.
: Well forgive me for coming all the way across town in the cold to spend time with you.
: I can not forgive you. But I can make you a bowl of delicious soup that will warm both your heart and your soul.
As you can see, I decided to spend the night hanging out at Tojo Ramen with Tsuneyo.
And despite the way she’s slowly waving a knife around, it’s clear that she is happy to see me.
Well, “happy” is probably a bit of an exaggeration.
But she was just standing around before I got here and is now capable of doing her job- the one thing in life she appears to be confident in.
: Just make me whatever you feel like making. I don’t care.
: I don’t feel like making anything. Are you okay with starving?
: You don’t feel like getting...closer to noodles or whatever?
scene tsuneyogreenonion4
: I will not be told to get closer to Noodles by the one man who stays as far away from him as possible.
: Not bird-noodles. Noodles-noodles.
: It’s unlike you to not want to cook.
scene tsuneyogreenonion5
: As a wise man once said...even the best fall down sometimes.
: That wasn’t a wise man. That’s the chorus from Howie Day’s 2003 hit single, “Collide.”
: And what a wise man he was.
: But who said it does not matter even half as much as what was said, Sensei.
: I’m afraid that I am just lacking the same motivation and excitement that you would normally come to expect from a lively, energetic girl like myself.
: Yes. Because when I think of Tsuneyo Tojo, I immediately think “lively.”
: If only I could be more like this knife.
: I know there’s a metaphor in there somewhere, but I’d appreciate it if you could just tell me what it is so I don’t have to use my brain.
: Sharp. And made of steel. This is the me who never was. The me who is not.
: If this is another comedy routine, I'm going to go ahead and do you a favor by asking you to scrap it.
scene tsuneyogreenonion6
: Gone...like noodles in the wind. Flying about and causing destruction everywhere they roam.
: This is the Tsuneyo Tojo you see before you. A shell of her former crab.
: What the hell happened to you overnight?
scene tsuneyogreenonion7
: Is this what they call “depression?” Should I see a doctor?
: I highly doubt that. Why don’t you just tell me what’s going on?
: I can’t guarantee that I can help or anything but, sometimes, talking about stuff is all you need to feel a little better.
: Also, if I’m on better terms with you, you won’t feel the urge to stab me with that knife you’re still waving around.
: How did you know about that urge? Did I mention it out loud in the heat of my sadness?
You know, maybe I should call it an early night and head back home before Ami needs to identify my body at the local morgue?
: Just tell me what’s wrong. That’s the least you can do to make up for not serving me while you’re still open.
: It’s either that or I leave you a bad Yelp review.
scene tsuneyogreenonion8
: Don’t you dare! Everyone knows that a restaurant’s success is entirely dependent on the thoughts of various inexperienced consumers who went through the effort of actually creating a Yelp account!
: I shall turn you into ramen, you bastard!
: Okay. On that note, I’m just going to-
scene tsuneyogreenonion1
: Fine. I will talk.
: But it is very sad. Please do not cry when you hear how horrible things are.
: I’m sure that I’ve heard worse than whatever it is you’re going through.
: Sigh.
: Sensei...
: It appears that the restaurant is out of green onions.
: Not to be mistaken with the Green Onion of the second floor. She has not yet come to this restaurant.
: And...that’s why you’re giving up on everything?
: One item being out of stock is a symbol of my failure as the acting manager of this business.
: First, it is the green onions. Then, it is chopsticks.
: Then, next thing I know, everyone has to grab their noodles with their fingers and eat them the way birds eat worms.
: Sure. Except birds don’t have fingers and use their beaks to eat.
scene tsuneyogreenonion8
: Oh, so now you care about what birds do? How dare you?
: Is that really all that’s bothering you? Running out of one thing?
scene tsuneyogreenonion1
: I was prepared to adapt to the situation at first...
: But as the hours went by and no customers entered the store, I realized that my failure must have already spread throughout the city.
: I’m afraid it is too late for me now.
: No one’s come in all day?
scene tsuneyogreenonion3
: If they have, they are either invisible or extremely sneaky. And not hungry.
: We have experienced slow days in the past, but never anything like this.
: Though, I am prepared to experience happiness once more if you offset the lack of profit by purchasing everything on the menu.
: You know...I would, but I was kind of hoping for something with green onions.
scene tsuneyogreenonion9
: Of course. Another reminder of my inadequacy makes itself known before the doors are closed for the night.
: Tojo Ramen is no more. This is the end.
: Oh, stop being dramatic.
scene tsuneyogreenonion10
: Dramatic?! Me?! The world is crashing down right now and you have the audacity to demand such a thing?!
: Where do you get off?!
: Jesus. There’s no need to yell.
scene tsuneyogreenonion3
: I apologize. I was attempting to show the difference between true drama and what you had labeled as drama, but my acting skills were so good that you must have gotten scared.
: Tsuneyo, you do realize there is a very easy way to solve your problem of not having onions, right?
: I’m sure customers won’t magically appear again once you obtain them, but it’s not like they are out of reach forever.
: Not forever. But we do not receive our next shipment of produce until two days from now.
: It is highly probable that I will have to sell my body to make up for the loss in profit we face during this time.
: There’s no way you’re losing that- wait.
: For what? Why am I waiting?
: Just out of curiosity...
: How much would you be selling it for?
: I am not sure. I do not even know what the process of selling one’s body entails. I just know that it is meant to generate a great amount of revenue.
: Oh. Well, uhh...that’s probably not an alternative you’ll have to worry about. Especially with this incredibly smart proposition I am about to...propose.
: If you are attempting to purchase me, I will give you a 5%% discount.
: A: Don’t even bother offering discounts that small. And B: Let’s go get you more green onions.
: Impossible. Produce delivery day is still 48 hours off. You are out of line, sir.
: I’m telling you that you don’t have to wait. You can just go to the convenience store and buy enough to hold you over for a day or two.
: Aren’t you supposed to be amazing at this? I’m surprised you didn’t think of that.
scene tsuneyogreenonion11
: It did not even occur to me.
: I finally understand where the word convenience in “convenience store” comes from.
: They are able to operate outside the jurisdiction of the Produce Delivery Administration.
: Yup. That’s exactly why they are called that.
: The only issue is that you’ll have to close the store while you’re out so people don’t wind up coming in and robbing the place.
scene tsuneyogreenonion1
: That is a fair price to pay. It is not as if anyone will enter the restaurant when it already reeks of failure to begin with.
: Now, we just need to locate one of the stores.
: There’s one that Noriko works at not far from here. We can just go there.
scene tsuneyogreenonion11
: Another convenience. Things are already beginning to turn around.
: Please give me a moment to check with my father and see if such a task is allowed.
: Do you really need permission? Aren’t you in charge of the place while he’s...sick?
scene tsuneyogreenonion3
: I am also worried that this may be a trap and that you are going to kidnap me and throw me into traffic.
: That’s not what human trafficking means, Tsuneyo.
: That may just be what you want me to think.
: I will return shortly.
: Please help yourself to some chopsticks while you wait.
scene black
: And do...what with them?...
scene tsuneyogreenonion12
Tsuneyo returns downstairs several minutes later and proceeds to shut off a bunch of the equipment in the restaurant.
It looks like she got permission to just close entirely rather than temporarily.
Now that I think about it, I’m not even really sure what time Tojo Ramen stays open until.
But given the fact that I was their first customer of the day on account of the invisible, yet noticeable aura of Tsuneyo’s “failure,” I can’t imagine anyone else was coming tonight.
We make our way through the old district as a series of homeless, decrepit onlookers gaze at us with a mix of curiosity and what could only be interpreted as desperation.
What they’re desperate for, I have no clue.
But I try not to think about it because...
Well, it’s fucking creepy.
: I have never walked around this area at night before.
: It is quite different than it is during the day.
: The people seem rather lively.
scene tsuneyogreenonion13
: This is lively to you?
: Compared to normal, I would say yes.
: Though these villagers likely lack both the physical and mental fortitude they possessed when they were younger, you can still sense the curiosity dwelling within them.
: I mean, it’s not really “sensing” it if they’re looking right at us.
: Where else would you ask they look instead?
: It is not a crime to simply watch.
: That kind of depends on what you’re watching, I think.
: If you spend too much time looking down on how others look at you, you will miss out on many of the beautiful things life has to offer.
: Branches...Leaves...The wide part...
: Those are all just different parts of a tree. I’m sure there is more in life that you think is beautiful.
scene tsuneyogreenonion14
: Of course.
: Those are just the first things that came to mind.
: My father has always kept trees close to his heart, so I assume I inherited that love from him.
: And these people- the ones staring at us as we venture forth toward produce-
: Even they are more lively than he is now.
: They can stand...and speak without the assistance of a machine.
: I knew he couldn’t walk, but...he can’t speak anymore either?
: Not the way you and I can.
: We are special. Gifted, even.
: But one day, that gift will be taken away from us.
: And we will wish in those final moments that we had not pushed so many of life’s beauties aside.
: So do not look at these people with unease clouding your mind. Look at them as worse or older versions of us.
: You do realize that way of wording it sounds even worse than the one I used, right?
scene tsuneyogreenonion15
: I would rather be acknowledged as a worse version of someone else than not acknowledged at all.
: Meet with your fears and learn that they are nothing worth fearing at all.
: Do not avert your gaze. For they will stop existing the moment you wish them to.
: Keep them alive. Because it is possible that one day, you will be in their shoes...
: Staring at a man and a woman making their way down the street- remembering when that used to be you.
: So, when do I get to meet your father?
: I do not think you ever will.
: Why not? That whole speech made it sound like you really want old people to be happy for whatever reason.
: And, who knows? Maybe he’d like my company?
: My father is a man full of pride.
: He does not wish to be seen in his current state.
: So, unless that changes, I will respect his wishes and continue to deliver quality noodle dishes to all of his loyal customers when I am not too busy failing them.
: Well, here’s hoping that obtaining the one missing ingredient in your store is enough to magically remind everyone that you exist again.
: Thanks, bro.
: If that does not work, I will look further into the process of body sales.
: Sure. As long as I’m the first person who gets a quote.
: You already received a quote earlier. From the wise man, Howard Daylight.
: Not...that kind of...
scene black
: Oh, fuck it.
